correctness.rationale: Two initially white vertices in an attached clique are permanent adjacent-twin obstructions, implying r-1 local selected vertices. For any zero forcing set, the activated-root projection is zero forcing in the original graph: an unactivated root cannot be forced by its deficient clique. This yields the exact lower bound. Explicit activation and base forcing establish sufficiency and every equality case. Each base fiber is a connected Cartesian product of K_r and K_(r+1); between-base edge counts are precisely (2r)^2 times the choices on shared roots, and every base edge lifts. This proves all component and edge formulas. Independent finite exhaustive bitmask and set-based programs reproduced minima and the graph data in their stated ranges.

value.rationale: The transformation works for every connected graph, allowing all minimum zero-forcing placements and their transition-component sizes to be transferred from G to its connected clique corona. It establishes an exact, nontrivial mobility invariant: connectivity and the number of components are preserved even while every component grows by a closed multiplicative factor. These properties are neither measured nor implied by the previously known optimum cardinality alone.
